name: JWT
hubBlurb: Decode a token's header and payload — reads, doesn't verify.
seoDescription: Decode a JWT's header and payload entirely offline — it never leaves your machine, and this tool doesn't verify signatures.
directAnswer: Umbra's JWT tool decodes a token's header and payload entirely offline — it never sends the token anywhere, and it doesn't verify signatures.
body: Paste a token to see its header and payload laid out clearly, with expiry and issued-at claims translated into plain language (“expires in 3 days,” not a raw timestamp). It reads the token; it doesn't check whether it's genuine — stated plainly in the tool itself.
screenshotAlt: Umbra's JWT tool showing a decoded token's header and payload.

faqs.q: Why not decode a JWT with a free online tool?
faqs.a: A JWT often carries real session or identity data — Umbra decodes entirely on your machine and never transmits it.
No, and it says so — verifying requires the signing key, which this tool never asks for.

faqs.q: Can it warn me if a token isn't signed?
faqs.a: Yes — Umbra flags a token as unsigned or using an unreadable algorithm, which means anyone could have created or altered it, before you read anything else on the page.
